accuracy.evidence: Checked against the English national curriculum Year 2 grammar appendix (how the grammatical patterns in a sentence indicate its function as a statement, question, exclamation or command), the KS1 English grammar, punctuation and spelling test framework definition that an exclamation starts with What or How and contains a verb, and Common Core L.1.1j (declarative, interrogative, imperative, exclamatory). Every sentence in the sorter, bossy verb rounds, question builds (Is the dog hungry? Can you swim?) and command builds was rechecked against those definitions; no one-word interjection is called an exclamation sentence.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1 grammar slips: typing a sentence by its end mark (Sit down! prediction and the sorter message for commands dropped in Exclamation), assuming the first word of a command is the bossy verb (Please shut the door. prediction, Carefully put the cup down. round), reading How tall you are! as a question because of How (sorter feedback and challenge tag how), making a question by only adding ? (Make a question prediction) and ending a question with a full stop (question builder feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagkinds models sentence function and the grammar that signals it: a four-way job sorter, an imperative-verb finder where the verb is not always first, subject-verb inversion to form a question, What/How exclamation starters and dropping the subject to form an imperative. flagstop is about capitals and choosing an end mark by sound, flagsent builds who plus doing-word sentences and flagqw is question words; none sorts by function or transforms between types. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The sorter rejects Sit down! in Exclamation with the reason, the bossy verb step only accepts shut or put after Please or Carefully, the question builder only accepts the verb first and the question mark at the end, the exclamation step only accepts What before a and How before an adjective or adverb, and the command step only lets you remove You. The child does each transformation before the done message states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, it has !' for Sit down!, 'Yes, Please' for the bossy verb, and 'Just put ? at the end' for making a question. The task straight after each makes the child act against the wrong choice and the done message quotes their guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own corrections: bang (ends with ! but has the bossy verb Shut), tell (a statement does a different job), how (starts with How but does not ask), bossyx (no bossy verb), stop (a full stop ends statements and commands), bangq (! ends exclamations or strong commands), bossyq (Get ready. is a command), first (Carefully tells how) and thing (paper is a noun). Lab taps also name the slip.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences with spoken examples (A question asks. Where is my hat?) and scores well under the family kid limit of 5.0; the adult text stays under 10 while using the exact curriculum terms statement, question, exclamation, command, function, imperative verb, subject, declarative, interrogative, imperative and exclamatory, and the codes Year 2 grammar appendix and L.1.1j.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph shows one sentence type with real examples, and the last shows the job-not-mark rule and a question transform; adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements, the form of each type, four named mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with the starting and ending sentences, building sentences and question words lessons stays under 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the four job boxes sit in a 2 by 2 grid about 165 px wide each, the sentence card spans the width with 17 px text, word tiles wrap into centred rows at least 44 px wide, the What/How/Is picks are three 76 px tiles, and the young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall. Nothing clips in light or dark.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone, no console errors, every Show me completed. Every canvas drag or tap has a button twin (one button per type, per word tile, per starter, with labels such as 'Bossy verb: shut' and 'Add question mark') and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'Yes! "shut" is the bossy verb. It does not have to come first.'
